sub_elements.quality_note: Key software tools identified: Human Protein Atlas deep learning model, node2vec (PPI embedding), MuSIC pipeline (integration), Cytoscape (community detection), IMP version 2.18 (structural modeling), FAIRSCAPE-CLI (packaging/validation). External resource link for IMP documentation.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Software documentation covers data processing pipeline: embedding generation (HPA model, node2vec), integration (MuSIC), community detection (Cytoscape), structural modeling (IMP 2.18), and packaging (FAIRSCAPE-CLI). Version specificity (IMP 2.18) and external documentation links enhance reproducibility. Could be strengthened with version numbers for other tools and GitHub repositories (mentioned in recommendations but not linked).

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: [13 entries including Nature publication, bioRxiv preprint, FAIRSCAPE documentation, IMP, NDEx, Bridge2AI, CFDE, MassIVE, SRA, Perturbation Cell Atlas publication]; cleaning_strategies: Gene Ontology (GO), Reactome, Protein Data Bank (PDB), AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, Schema.org, EVI Evidence Graph Ontology; conforms_to: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema/core-schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive external standards and resources: publications (Nature, bioRxiv), ontologies (GO, Reactome, EVI), databases (PDB, AlphaFoldDB), repositories (MassIVE, SRA, NDEx), frameworks (FAIRSCAPE, Schema.org, Bridge2AI), and schema conformance (D4D Core).
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: External standards semantically comprehensive: scientific publications for methods/results, biological ontologies for annotation (GO, Reactome), structural databases for modeling (PDB, AlphaFoldDB), domain repositories for data deposition (MassIVE for proteomics, SRA for genomics, NDEx for networks), and metadata standards (Schema.org, EVI, D4D). Multi-level integration of community standards.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: discouraged_uses: [Use During Incomplete Data Release - interim/beta release with data not in completed final form, some datasets under pre-publication embargo, protein interrogation sets incompletely overlap across data modalities, computed cell maps not yet included; Analysis Without Domain Expertise - requires domain expertise for meaningful analysis, most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of individual datasets]
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations documented in discouraged_uses field: dataset is interim/beta (not final), incomplete overlaps across modalities, missing computed cell maps in current release, requires domain expertise for analysis. Honest disclosure of work-in-progress status.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Limitations disclosure semantically honest and actionable: temporal limitation (beta through November 2026), data completeness limitation (incomplete modality overlap, missing computed maps), and expertise limitation (bioinformatics/functional genomics knowledge required). Users can make informed decisions about dataset maturity and suitability.

sub_elements.name: Systematic Biases Identified and Described
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: Data derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants in the population at large; sampling_strategies: is_representative: false; instances: MDA-MB-468 from 51-year-old black female, KOLF2.1J from healthy male Northern European donor
sub_elements.quality_note: Bias explicitly acknowledged: cell lines do not represent population-level biological diversity (is_representative: false). Donor demographics documented (51-year-old black female for MDA-MB-468, healthy male Northern European for KOLF2.1J) enabling users to assess representativeness for their research questions.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Bias documentation semantically appropriate: explicit statement of non-representativeness (is_representative: false), rationale (commercially available cell lines selected for disease relevance, not population sampling), and donor demographics for context. Purposive sampling strategy clearly distinguished from representative sampling.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: No dedicated anomalies field; preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies describe quality control procedures
sub_elements.quality_note: No specific data anomalies or quality issues documented. Quality control procedures described (standardized protocols, validation before release) but no discussion of known data quality problems, outliers, or technical artifacts.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Core schema may not include anomalies field available in full schema. Quality control procedures suggest attention to data quality, but lack of explicit anomaly documentation means users cannot anticipate specific issues (e.g., failed experiments, technical artifacts, outlier samples).

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: Cell Line Origin Metadata - metadata about cell line origins (age, sex, race of original donor) is retained for scientific context but does not constitute identifiable human subjects data; discouraged_uses: Clinical Decision-Making Without Validation - laboratory data from cell lines are not to be used in clinical decision-making or any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitive content identified: cell line origin metadata (donor demographics) explicitly noted as non-identifiable but sensitive. Content warning for clinical use: explicitly prohibited without regulatory approval and clinical validation.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Sensitive content disclosure semantically appropriate: transparency about retained origin metadata, clear distinction between research-grade and clinical-grade data, explicit prohibition on clinical decision-making. Protects against misuse while enabling scientific context.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research: De-identification confirmed by CM4AI Ethics Module and Data Access Committee; maintainers: Ethical Review by Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca); creators: Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon (Ethics Module Leader), Vardit Ravitsky (Ethics Module)
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics review documented with responsible individuals (Vardit Ravitsky at The Hastings Center, Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon at Simon Fraser University), institutional affiliations, and contact information. Data Access Committee oversight for distribution ethics. No explicit conflicts of interest statement.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Ethics review semantically credible: dedicated Ethics Module, external ethics experts (bioethicist at The Hastings Center), Data Access Committee for distribution oversight. Contact information enables stakeholder engagement. Absence of explicit conflicts of interest statement is minor gap but not critical for cell line data.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: University of California San Diego; distribution_formats: University of Virginia Dataverse (instance of Harvard's Dataverse, an NIH-approved generalist repository); external_resources: University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/DXWOS5
sub_elements.quality_note: Published on recognized institutional repository: University of Virginia's LibraData (Dataverse instance), which is NIH-approved. Long-term preservation supported by committed institutional funds. Also distributed via domain-specific platforms (MassIVE for proteomics, NCBI SRA for sequencing, NDEx for networks).
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Platform choice semantically appropriate: NIH-approved repository (Dataverse) for long-term preservation, domain-specific repositories for data types (MassIVE, SRA, NDEx), and project-specific portal (cm4ai.org). Multi-platform strategy maximizes findability and accessibility.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/DXWOS5; license_and_use_terms: Any publications referencing this data or derived products should cite the Nature article (Schaffer LV, Hu M, et al. 2025. doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3) and the bioRxiv preprint (Clark T, et al. 2024. doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311) and directly cite the data collection.
sub_elements.quality_note: DOI for dataset (10.18130/V3/DXWOS5) and recommended citations for associated publications (Nature article, bioRxiv preprint). Citation guidance specifies citing both publications and data collection directly.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Citation framework semantically complete: dataset DOI for data citation, publication DOIs for methods/results citation, explicit requirement to cite data collection. Nature publication (peer-reviewed, high-impact) and bioRxiv preprint provide scientific context.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema/core-schema; cleaning_strategies: Data mapped to applicable standards and ontologies including Gene Ontology (GO), Reactome, Protein Data Bank (PDB), AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, Schema.org, and EVI Evidence Graph Ontology; distribution_formats: RO-Crate packages with JSON-LD using Schema.org and EVI vocabularies
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple community standards: D4D Core schema for metadata, RO-Crate for FAIR packaging, GO/Reactome for functional annotation, PDB/AlphaFoldDB for structural data, Schema.org for web semantics, EVI for provenance. Keywords mapped to controlled vocabularies (NCI Thesaurus, BioAssay Ontology, Cell Ontology, CHEBI, EFO).
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Community standards conformance semantically comprehensive: metadata standard (D4D Core), packaging standard (RO-Crate), biological ontologies (GO, Reactome), structural databases (PDB, AlphaFoldDB), web semantics (Schema.org), provenance ontology (EVI), and term vocabularies (NCI Thesaurus, etc.). Multi-layered standards integration demonstrates FAIR commitment.

sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: [CM4AI Project Website https://www.cm4ai.org, NIH RePORTER Project Details, FAIRSCAPE Framework Documentation https://fairscape.github.io, Integrative Modeling Platform http://integrativemodeling.org, Network Data Exchange https://www.ndexbio.org, Bridge2AI Program https://commonfund.nih.gov/bridge2ai, NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem https://www.nih-cfde.org]

Tasks field mentions 'CM4AI Skills and Workforce Development module' for training resources.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: Outreach materials semantically diverse: project landing page (cm4ai.org), technical documentation (FAIRSCAPE, IMP), data visualization (NDEx), funding transparency (NIH RePORTER), community context (Bridge2AI, CFDE), and training resources (Skills/Workforce Development module). Multi-stakeholder engagement strategy.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.evidence: No related_datasets field present in core schema; distributions field mentions multiple version DOIs but not as typed relationships
sub_elements.quality_note: Core schema does not include related_datasets field. Multiple dataset versions mentioned (V1.4, V2.1, October 2025 Beta) but not formalized as typed relationships (isVersionOf, hasPart, etc.). External publications reference related datasets (Perturbation Cell Atlas) but not machine-readable.
sub_elements.semantic_analysis: CoreDataset class excludes related_datasets field present in full schema. Version relationships could be formalized (e.g., V2.1 isVersionOf V1.4) but are currently narrative in distributions field. Perturbation Cell Atlas publication mentions related dataset but not linked with typed relationship.

strengths: Exceptionally comprehensive description (1,180+ chars) with specific details on cell lines, data modalities, computational pipelines, and publications
Outstanding funding transparency with NIH grant numbers (1OT2OD032742-01, 5U54HG012513-02), budget details ($5.3M FY2025), and timeline (2022-2026)
Robust version management with distinct DOIs for each quarterly beta release (V1.4, V2.1, October 2025) and detailed change descriptions
Comprehensive technical transparency: 4 collection mechanisms, 4 acquisition methods, 6 preprocessing strategies, 2 cleaning strategies with specific tools, versions, and responsible laboratories
Extensive creator documentation (24 entries) with ORCIDs, institutional affiliations, and module leadership roles

Strong community integration: multiple standards (D4D Core, RO-Crate, GO, Reactome, PDB, AlphaFoldDB, Schema.org, EVI), repositories (Dataverse, MassIVE, SRA, NDEx), and outreach (project website, FAIRSCAPE docs, IMP docs)
27 diverse keywords providing excellent semantic coverage across biological entities, methods, standards, and diseases
Honest limitations disclosure: interim/beta status, incomplete modality overlaps, missing computed cell maps, domain expertise requirements, non-representative sampling

Appropriate ethics framework for cell line data: explicit non-human subjects status, de-identification confirmed by Ethics Module and Data Access Committee, sensitive content warnings for clinical misuse
Multi-platform distribution strategy: NIH-approved Dataverse for long-term preservation, domain repositories (MassIVE, SRA, NDEx) for data types, project portal (cm4ai.org) for outreach
weaknesses: Core schema lacks parent_datasets and related_datasets fields available in full schema, limiting machine-readable relationship documentation
No dedicated known_limitations field - limitations discussed in discouraged_uses but not as structured element
No explicit data anomalies or quality issues documented despite beta status and incomplete data overlaps
No dedicated known_biases field - bias acknowledged (is_representative: false) but not in structured element
Software tool documentation lacks version numbers (except IMP 2.18) and GitHub repository links for MuSIC pipeline, node2vec implementation, and other custom tools
No explicit conflicts of interest statement, though ethics review structure is documented
Variable metadata not applicable (is_tabular: false) limits structured data dictionary accessibility
Related datasets (Perturbation Cell Atlas, related Bridge2AI projects) mentioned in prose but not formalized as typed relationships
recommendations: Add structured known_limitations and known_biases fields in future full schema version to complement narrative discussions in discouraged_uses and sensitive_elements
Document specific data anomalies or quality issues if any exist (failed experiments, technical artifacts, outliers) to enable users to anticipate and handle edge cases
Include version numbers for all software tools (Human Protein Atlas model, node2vec, MuSIC pipeline, Cytoscape) and provide GitHub repository links for custom code to enhance reproducibility
Add explicit conflicts of interest statement for all creators and funders to strengthen ethical transparency
Formalize version relationships using typed links (e.g., V2.1 isVersionOf V1.4, V2.1 replaces V1.4) in future full schema implementation
Link related datasets (Perturbation Cell Atlas bioRxiv, related Bridge2AI projects) with typed relationships when using full schema
Consider adding RRID identifiers for key resources beyond cell lines (antibodies from Human Protein Atlas, 10x Genomics kit, etc.) to enhance resource citation

Expand quality control documentation with specific acceptance criteria, rejection rates, or quality metrics (e.g., imaging quality thresholds, MS identification confidence scores) to enable users to assess data reliability
